title: Divergence: forge certifies L3 for a StructLit door-bypass — the IFC abstraction barrier is missing (06-provenance-and-sinks.md REQ-2; R-DEFER-9)

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content:
Failing tests at forge/tests/divergence_provenance.rs pin the StructLit door-bypass on all 3 IFC axes (#[ignore]d behind this blocker; un-ignore when fixed):
- taint_structlit_bypass_must_not_certify_l3: query(Sql { stmt: input.raw }) from a Tainted -> certifies L3 (must be L0)
- secret_structlit_bypass_must_not_certify_l3: emit(Public { val: s.val }) from a Secret -> L3 (must be L0)
- capability_structlit_bypass_must_not_certify_l3: delete(Authorized { id: u.id }) from a User -> L3 (must be L0)

REPRODUCED live (real forge + verus 0.2026.05.24): each bypass_* fn certifies L3, exit 0. The naive control path (query(input)/emit(s)/delete(u)) correctly stays L0 — so v1 catches the NAIVE form but NOT the StructLit launder. cargo test --workspace 488 passed / 0 failed; clippy + fmt clean.

ROOT CAUSE: NO abstraction barrier. The clean types (Sql/Public/Authorized) are ordinary Stage-1 newtype structs with ACCESSIBLE fields, so an Expr::StructLit (Sql { stmt: input.raw }) outside the declared #[boundary] door mints a clean type directly from a marked value. v1's 'emergent type-level enforcement' relied on the type system, but the type system does NOT prevent constructing a clean struct from a tainted/secret/unauthorized field. This is a R-DEFER-9 launder: a marked value reaches the sink as clean without the door, obligation silently dropped.

This DIRECTLY violates 06-provenance-and-sinks.md REQ-2 ('No mark-change exists outside a door — a value's mark is fixed at construction (the struct literal) and changeable only by passing a door's return type') and cases.json ('the ONLY door from a marked type to a clean type is the declared #[boundary] door'). The handled-or-loud law is broken: the forbidden flow is neither handled (no door) nor loud (no L0) — it is silently certified L3.

FIX DIRECTION (do NOT fix here — generator's job): an ABSTRACTION BARRIER. Either (a) a sealed / door-only-constructible clean type — the validator rejects an Expr::StructLit of a clean type outside its declared #[boundary] door (the type is constructible only via its door's return), OR (b) the v1.1 dataflow-propagation engine (REQ-4) — a StructLit reading a Tainted/Secret field yields a marked result, rejected at the sink. Either makes the door the only launder point.

R-SPEC-4 DOC-CORRECTION (overstated v1 claim): 06-provenance-and-sinks.md asserts v1 makes injection 'un-typeable' and is 'EMERGENT from SHIPPED machinery, NO new validator code'. With the StructLit hole that is FALSE for v1 — v1 catches ONLY the naive direct-source form. The 'un-typeable' guarantee requires the abstraction barrier, which is NEW validator code, not emergent. The doc's v1/v1.1 line is mis-drawn: the barrier is not v1.1 dataflow nicety, it is REQUIRED for the v1 centerpiece to hold. Amend the doc (acto-doc-author) to either pull the barrier into v1 scope or stop claiming v1 is un-typeable.

COVERAGE GAP: forge/tests/provenance_conformance.rs tests ONLY the naive careless path (query(input)); it never exercises the StructLit launder — which is why the hole shipped green.

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content: Pin the StructLit door-bypass as 3 #[ignore]d failing tests in forge/tests/divergence_provenance.rs (one per IFC axis), asserting the authority's required behavior (un-doored marked->clean flow must be L0, never L3). Commit the failing-test artifact on main; the fixer un-ignores when the abstraction barrier lands. No production code touched (critic role).

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content:
FIXED by the #[sealed] ABSTRACTION BARRIER (06-provenance-and-sinks.md REQ-8) at commit 5f8b55df.

WHAT LANDED: AST StructItem.sealed: bool (ast.rs); parser parse_attribute -> ParsedAttr::Sealed routed onto a struct by parse_item (parse_struct(start, sealed)), #[sealed] on enum/fn/spec fn is a parse error; validator Validator::new collects sealed_structs, NEW SpecError::SealedConstruction { name, span }, check_sealed_construction rejects any Expr::StructLit of a sealed struct from BOTH walk arms (exec scan_expr_for_loops + caged walk_expr_inner). Consumer pub fn validate -> forge::check::check_file (ForgeError::Spec, exit non-zero, no L3). Corpus: Sql/Public/Authorized marked #[sealed] in conformance/provenance_demo.th.

VERIFICATION (real forge + verus): the 3 pinned #77 bypass tests UN-IGNORED + PASS -- query(Sql{stmt:input.raw}) / emit(Public{val:s.val}) / delete(Authorized{id:u.id}) each REJECTED with SealedConstruction (no L3). Safe doored paths STILL L3 (door is foreign external_body, no in-language StructLit). Naive careless still L0. Plain non-sealed structs unaffected (rule is opt-in + inert). StructItem.sealed broke no downstream exhaustive match (only parser constructs it; lower reads name/fields/inv only -- a sealed struct lowers identically).

GAUNTLET: cargo build --workspace OK; cargo test --workspace 500 passed / 0 failed / 0 ignored; clippy -D warnings PASS; fmt --check PASS. REQ-8 NOT-STARTED -> SHIPPED in the doc + validator //! table; REQ-1..REQ-7 stay NOT-STARTED (owned by #76).
